# Language Models: From N-grams to Neural Networks {#sec-language-models}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon="false"}
**Chapter status: skeleton.**
:::

**Learning objectives.** After this chapter you can:

- define a language model as a probability distribution over sequences;
- estimate an n-gram model by counting, and explain why it breaks;
- explain perplexity and compute it on a toy corpus;
- describe how neural LMs share statistical strength through embeddings.

## The counting era

<!-- TODO(draft): chain rule of probability; Markov assumption; MLE by
     counting — this is the chapter where the statistics audience feels at
     home, lean into it. Smoothing as regularization. -->

A language model is nothing exotic: [a probability distribution over the
next token given the ones before it]{.hl}. The whole modern stack is a
sequence of increasingly good estimators of that same distribution.
